chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Mufaddal ibn Ibrahim ibn Qays ibn Rumana al-Ash'ari, Sa'dan ibn Ishaq ibn Sa'id, Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Malik, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qatawani all narrated to us, saying: Hasan ibn Mahbub al-Zarrad narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Ammar al-Sayrafi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah saying:
There was a set time for this matter, and it was in the year forty and one hundred [140 AH], but when you announced it and made it public, Allah delayed it.

key_terms.أَذَعْتُمُوهُ: You made it public/announced it widely
key_terms.الْأَمْر: The matter (referring to the rise/appearance of the Imam)

ai.seo_question: Why was the appearance of the Qa'im delayed according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the year 104 AH as the appointed time for the Qa'im's appearance, noting that the premature publicity by his followers caused God to delay the event. This narration is central to the Shia doctrine of 'Takhir' (postponement), illustrating how human actions, specifically excessive announcement, can influence the timing of the Occultation.
